# OpenCareQ (v4.0.0)

> Non-commercial NHS-first clinical quantum & upstream prevention workbench (`phi_present = False`; `PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0` / `CC BY-NC-SA 4.0` / 15-Year UK Database Right `SI 1997/3032`; stewarded via `INALYN Community Interest Company #17398798`). Across all `42` statutory NHS England Integrated Care Boards (`1,280` PCNs, `62,925,110` registered patients), OpenCareQ `v4.0.0` achieves `400 / 400` (`100%`) zero-fit clinical & structural parity across `80` verified RCSB PDB crystal/neutron structures (`#80` = `2026` `PDB: 10QV`), `3,024` deterministic `NHS DCB0129` safety evaluations (`216` paired `G1-G108` cases, `Youden's J = 1.000`, `0` gated harms), a `15.2802 ZiB` `(40e, 38o)` sulfonium-heme `MPO` `ACQ Gate G4` benchmark, `49` `NIST FIPS 204 ML-DSA-65` sealed receipts, and `+£19,069.84M/yr` (`+£19.07B/yr`) in strict `NICE PMG36 NHS/PSS` equity-weighted value (`£0` DWP/employer transfer inflation; `£0` NHS software licensing cost). Statutory boundary: OpenCareQ operates strictly in clinician- and pharmacist-in-charge Shadow Mode — it is not a certified medical device, is not clinically validated for autonomous patient care, never replaces clinician judgment, has zero autonomous prescribing approved, and claims zero proven physical QPU speedup today (`csc_qt_numerical_score_computed = None`; all `7` hazards `H-OCQ-01..07` `OPEN`). For the complete self-contained machine-readable corpus, read [llms-full.txt](https://arunnadarasa.github.io/opencareq-nhs/llms-full.txt).
